decisions.question: Is closing the goto->break gap on 1after909::doit SMALL (one option-gated Action/Rule) or LARGE (proposal fork)?
decisions.rationale: Two HARD RULE 7 triggers fire: (1) closing the gap requires porting Ghidra's BlockGraph::scopeBreak(-1,-1) -- an explicitly-recorded SEAM stub (losses.md; blockaction.rs:3493/3502) that is a recursive walk over the already-collapsed structured tree re-tagging loop-exit BlockGoto edges with f_break_goto/f_continue_goto -- which is touching S8 structuring code inside ActionFinalStructure::apply well beyond a single gated early-return; (2) it needs new ported-core methods in block.rs (scopeBreak, getExitLeaf, scope/loop-bottom plumbing) plus a printer change in printc.rs, i.e. >1 new module-level addition mutating structured-tree state, not modelable as one isolated Rule. The region/loop structure is already recovered (BlockWhileDo + f_loop_exit_edge exist), so this restores a missing upstream print-prep pass rather than inventing new condition refinement -- but it is still a structuring-stage port, which precedent (every prior S8 gap) and the rule both classify as a proposal.
decisions.owning_stage: S8 structuring -- decompiler/crates/kuna-decomp/src/s8_structure/blockaction.rs (ActionFinalStructure::apply, the graph.scopeBreak(-1,-1) SEAM at ~line 3493-3512) plus the supporting recursive method in decompiler/crates/kuna-decomp/src/substrate/block.rs and the print-emit in s9_emit/printc.rs
decisions.angr_reference: angr Phoenix/SAILR structurer break/continue recovery (loop successor refinement that lowers loop-exit gotos to break/continue); upstream-equivalent is Ghidra BlockGraph::scopeBreak
decisions.speed_risk: Negligible: one extra single-pass O(blocks) recursive walk of the structured block tree at finalize time, run once per function.
